transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, things at work have just been really getting to me lately. Ever since they made me the acting workflow lead, I've been walking into the warehouse already tense. It's like I'm just on edge the whole shift. I find myself snapping over little SAP errors, things that wouldn't have bothered me before. And I'm missing cycle-count deadlines, which I never used to do. Then, by the time I get home, I'm just too drained to do anything. I don't even have the energy to play basketball or work on my sketches anymore.
Have you lost interest in playing basketball or working on your sketches, or do you still enjoy them when you have the energy?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's hard to tell. I just... I haven't even tried to do either of them lately. By the time I clock out and get home, I'm just so beat that I usually just crash on the couch. So I don't really know if the interest is actually gone, or if I just don't have the gas left in the tank to find out.
On average, how many days a week would you say you feel down or sad, and does this feeling tend to linger throughout the day?

I don't really feel down or sad, honestly. It's more just... stress and being completely worn out. I wouldn't say I have days where I'm sitting around feeling depressed, I'm just constantly tense at work and then exhausted when I get home.
Do you ever experience feelings of anxiety, like your heart racing, trouble catching your breath, or a sense that things are closing in on you—especially at work?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. My heart doesn't race or anything, and I can breathe fine. It's not really a panicky feeling, just... like I said, I'm just tense and on edge the whole time I'm there. But no, no racing heart or feeling like things are closing in.
Outside of work, do you find yourself worrying a lot about other things—like your relationships, health, or other responsibilities—or do your anxious feelings mostly stay contained to your job?

No, it's pretty much just work. I don't really sit around worrying about my health or my relationships or anything like that. When I'm not at the warehouse, I'm just tired, but I'm not... I'm not really stressed about other stuff. It's just the job that keeps me on edge.
Do you find yourself caught up in constant worry about work, even when you're not at the warehouse, or is your tension mostly something that starts up again only when you're actually there?

No, I don't really sit around worrying about it when I'm at home. I mean, I dread going in the next day, but I'm not obsessing over it or anything. The real tension, that feeling of being totally on edge, that really only hits me when I'm actually there at the warehouse. Once I'm home, I'm just too exhausted to even think about it.
When you're at work and feeling tense, do you also find yourself getting more irritable or angry than usual?

Yeah, I definitely do. Ever since they made me the acting workflow lead, I’ve been walking into the warehouse already tense. And... yeah, I end up snapping over little SAP errors, just stuff that normally wouldn't bother me. It's really throwing me off. I'm even missing cycle-count deadlines that I never used to miss. And then I just go home completely drained. I'm too exhausted to even play basketball or work on my sketches anymore.
When you're at work, do you feel detached from your job or like you're just going through the motions, even if you're still technically doing your tasks?

No, I wouldn't say I feel detached. It's actually kind of the opposite. I'm not just zoning out or going through the motions... I'm way too keyed up for that. Like I mentioned, I'm getting actively frustrated and snapping at every little error that pops up. So, no, I definitely feel connected to what's happening, it's just... it's just really stressing me out.
Do you often feel emotionally drained by your work to the point that you have nothing left to give, or feel like you’re dealing with it in a detached, mechanical way?

Well, like I was just saying, I definitely don't feel detached or mechanical about it. I mean, I do go home completely drained, yeah, but it's more of a physical exhaustion from being so stressed and on edge all shift. I'm not... emotionally empty or just going through the motions. I'm still reacting to everything, just in a really frustrated way.
Do you feel like you're not performing as well at work as you used to, or like you're struggling to get things done even though you're putting in the same effort?

Yeah, I definitely am struggling. Like I mentioned before, I'm missing those cycle-count deadlines now. My supervisor actually had to bring it up during a performance check-in recently, which... that's never happened to me before. I used to be really on top of things. And it's not just at the warehouse. It feels like work is just taking over my whole life, because I'm not even showing up for basketball anymore, and I've completely stopped my sketching time. I just don't have the energy for any of it.
When you're not at work, do you still find yourself feeling anxious or worried about work-related things, even when there's no immediate problem to deal with?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, once I clock out, I'm not really sitting at home stressing about the warehouse or inventory counts. I don't really think about work when I'm not there. It's just that, like I was saying, I'm so wiped out from the shift that I just don't do anything else. But I'm not actively worrying about work stuff on my own time.
Would you say your irritability and frustration at work have become more frequent or intense over time, or do they tend to stay about the same each day?

I haven't really noticed it getting worse, to be honest. It... it feels like it just stays about the same each day. Every time I go in, it's just that same steady level of frustration. I wouldn't say it's building up or getting more intense over time, it's just kind of always there when I'm on the floor.
Do you often feel overwhelmed by your job responsibilities, like no matter how hard you try, it's never quite good enough or you can't keep up?

I wouldn't really say I feel overwhelmed like that. I mean, it's not that I feel like my work isn't good enough, or that the job itself is too much to handle. It's just... like I said before, I'm just really drained and frustrated when I'm there. But the actual responsibilities? No, I don't feel overwhelmed by them.
Do you feel like you're not accomplishing as much at work as you used to, or like your efforts aren't leading to any real success or progress?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean, my supervisor actually had to bring it up recently during a performance check-in. He pointed out that I've been missing some of my cycle-count deadlines, which... isn't usually like me. It just feels like work is taking over everything. Even when I'm not there, it's affecting me. I've completely stopped showing up for my regular basketball games, and I haven't even picked up my sketchbook in weeks. I just don't have the energy for any of it anymore.
Do you ever feel like you can't control your worry about work, even when you want to focus on something else?

No, I wouldn't say I worry about it like that. It's not like I'm sitting at home stressing over the inventory or feeling anxious and unable to stop thinking about the warehouse. It's really just... I'm completely drained by it. So when I want to focus on something else, it's not worry that gets in the way, it's just that I don't have the energy to do anything.
Do you feel like your job is making you feel emotionally exhausted, and do you feel less accomplished or effective in your role than you used to?

I think I pretty much just answered that. Like I said, I'm definitely drained by it—emotionally, physically, all of it. And yeah, my supervisor already pointed out that I'm missing deadlines, so I guess I am less effective than I used to be. It's just taking a lot out of me.
